Chip Industry Week In Review

23

$2B foundry pact; hyper-NA EUV; TSMC, Samsung financials; Canon readies nanoimprint; AI chips under scrutiny; $10T data center buildout; $1.5B SiC boost; chip smuggling; 800V power gains traction; quantum HW scales up; wireless EV road charging; sub-nm gate dielectrics; mobile fab.

October 9th, 2026 -

By: The SE Staff

Top of the Week

TSMC and GF inked a $2B manufacturing agreement, under which GF will manufacture silicon interposers for TSMC’s CoWoS advanced-packaging ecosystem at its Malta, New York fab. Volume production is expected to ramp in the first half of 2028.
Applied Materials and Intel are expanding their R&D collaboration to develop next-gen transistors, interconnects, and advanced packaging technologies, combining work at Applied’s EPIC Center in Silicon Valley with Intel’s R&D operations in Hillsboro, Oregon.
Rapidus launched Rapidus CORE, a global ecosystem framework intended to support customers from chip design through manufacturing for its planned 2nm foundry business. The first phase includes 17 design-service partners.
Xanadu and GF formed a multi-year manufacturing partnership to move ultra-low-loss silicon nitride photonics and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors onto GF’s 300mm production line in Malta, New York.

Big hauls

Wolfspeed received a conditional commitment for up to $1.5B in 30-year U.S. government financing to expand domestic SiC materials and wide-bandgap power-device production.
Vinci raised $250M in Series B funding at a $1.5B valuation to expand its AI-powered physics simulation platform. The platform models thermal, thermo-mechanical, and fluid behavior during design, with simulations reportedly running in minutes rather than hours or days.
Oratomic raised $475M for its neutral-atom quantum computing hardware.
VEIR raised $110M for superconducting power delivery technology for AI data centers.
Atomic Machines launched with $250M for its Matter Compiler system that builds micro-machines from code, including an electromechanical micro-relay to cut power in 800VDC data centers during a fault.

Financials

TSMC (Sept. revenue) and Samsung (Q3 guidance).

Analysis

Global semiconductor sales reached $159.7B in August, up 8% from July, with year-to-date sales topping $1T, reports SIA/WSTS.
McKinsey expects inference to account for about 60% of AI compute by 2030, driving demand for custom accelerators, HBM, chiplets, advanced packaging, and silicon photonics.
Silicon photonics, CPO, and optical networking are emerging as the next U.S.–China semiconductor battleground as AI data centers outgrow electrical interconnects, says Wilson Center, which estimates China accounts for 56% of global optical-transceiver manufacturing capacity.
Brookings estimates the U.S. AI buildout could require $10.3T through 2032 for data centers, power, networking and specialized chips, but it warned that increasingly complex financing could obscure financial risks.

Lithography

ASML and Carl Zeiss researchers outlined a hyper-NA EUV lithography architecture with a numerical aperture of at least 0.75, potentially enabling features as small as 5nm, more than one-third smaller than current high-NA systems. The technology could be ready in about a decade, although commercial production remains uncommitted.
Canon says its nanoimprint lithography technology is entering the final stage toward full-scale mass production.
DUV immersion lithography is the strongest remaining chokepoint on China’s AI-chip production, contends think tank Center for Technology & Statecraft. It estimates Chinese-owned fabs had accumulated more than 330 DUVi systems by 1Q26 and says continued imports could significantly narrow the U.S.-allied AI-chip manufacturing advantage. The report calls for a China-wide ban on DUVi exports, servicing restrictions and tighter controls on critical components.

Memory

Samsung is reportedly planning ~$3.9B in investment in memory-chip testing facilities in Vietnam.
Netlist and Micron entered into patent license and settlement agreements covering Netlist’s portfolio for server DIMMs and high-bandwidth memory, ending all pending legal proceedings between the companies.
Micron faces a potential walkout at its Taiwan facilities after workers voted overwhelmingly to authorize a strike over profit sharing.
Toshiba plans to invest approximately $380M to double HDD production capacity for AI data centers by fiscal 2027, compared with 2025 levels, reports Nikkei Asia.

Security and export controls

Arteris won an additional $3.3M through the U.S. government’s Trusted and Assured Microelectronics initiative to expand its third-party IP (3PIP) security assurance program in collaboration with BAE and SiFive.
The U.S. DOJ charged the owner of California-based Earthmade Computer with allegedly smuggling more than $300M in export-controlled computer servers to China. Prosecutors allege the servers contained high-end U.S.-manufactured GPUs and were routed through Malaysia and Singapore using false end-user and destination information to evade U.S. export controls.
Meanwhile, CSET researchers modeled more than 10 million scenarios for detecting diverted AI chips and found ping-based location verification to be the most cost-effective approach. However, they cautioned that implementation costs and complexity could limit its usefulness, and said that combining PLV with targeted physical inspections could improve enforcement.

Recognition

Silvaco CEO Wally Rhines was inducted into the National Academy of Engineering for his co-invention of the blue-light-emitting diode and decades of leadership in the semiconductor/EDA industry.

Global
Europe

SEMI Europe joined the European Commission’s new STEAM Executive Panel to represent semiconductor workforce needs and advise on industry-education partnerships, STEM participation, re-skilling, and up-skilling.
In Germany, X-FAB broke ground on a new cleanroom in Erfurt, and Mitutoyo opened a new semiconductor measurement and inspection center in Dresden.
HCSS warns that Europe risks losing its strong position in polysilicon unless production capacity grows fast enough to meet rising domestic and global demand.

Asia

Elephantech plans to open an advanced packaging center in Tokyo in March to support process development, prototyping, and scale-up for AI-server packaging and PCBs.
AMD is working with 14 South Korean AI semiconductor and technology companies to develop heterogeneous computing systems that combine AMD CPUs and GPUs with Korean AI processors, reports SBS News.
Cadence and Jilin University unveiled their CAE Multiphysics Joint Laboratory in China. The organizations also have a computational fluid dynamics joint lab.
Towa plans to invest approximately $32M in a new molding equipment plant near Kyoto, Japan, to expand production capacity for advanced packaging.

Americas

Nvidia, AMD, Micron, and eight other companies committed a combined $2.4B in AI tools and compute credits to the U.S. government’s Genesis Mission.
CSIS examines the trade-offs between restricting exports of U.S. AI technology and expanding global adoption of American chips and models, recommending targeted export controls and faster domestic innovation.
Draper broke ground on a 111,000 square-foot design, manufacturing, and advanced packaging facility in Massachusetts.
San Francisco enacted a 45-day moratorium on building or expanding data centers while the board looks at energy, water, air quality, land use, and community impacts, per NBC.

Reports and Deals
Patent agreement

Qualcomm and Huawei signed a multi-year patent cross-licensing agreement covering 5G, compute, AI, and networking. Qualcomm will separately acquire certain Huawei U.S. patents, pending regulatory approval.

M&A

Microchip acquired Vorago Technologies, maker of rad-hard, rad-tolerant MCUs and MPUs.
Skyworks completed its combination with Qorvo.
Navitas Semiconductor completed its acquisition of IVR maker Claros.
Cirrus Logic acquired INVENTVM, an Italian fabless chip company specializing in mixed-signal power-management and audio ICs.
Infineon completed its acquisition of C2i Semiconductors, adding software-defined multiphase controllers, smart power stages and vertical power-delivery expertise for AI data centers while expanding its power-systems R&D presence in India.

Suppliers Bet on VCSEL NPO (TrendForce)

New Technologies
EDA

Keysight added agentic AI to its design software, enabling engineers to connect AI agents to RF tools for circuit generation, verification, and optimization. ADS 2027 converts graphical RF designs into machine-readable representations and lets agents learn repeatable engineering workflows, addressing the inconsistent way LLMs interpret schematics and layouts.
Silicon Labs expanded its edge AI developer platform with SDKs and design intelligence.

Test

Teradyne added burn-in capabilities to its Titan HP system-level test platform, allowing high-power AI and other reliability-sensitive devices to be stressed under realistic workloads while controlling junction temperature and power at each device rather than using conventional burn-in ovens.
Keysight and research institutions developed a new measurement approach for continuous on-wafer characterization of sub-THz semiconductor devices. The company also introduced its Velocity 4900 Series aimed at test lab modernization for AI, enabling engineers to integrate physical test environments into automated CI/CD workflows.

Data center

Infineon launched a new 27kW three-phase PSU solution for AI data centers.
Microchip and Navitas collaborated on an 800V-to-6V reference design for OCP rack power development for 800VDC data centers.
NovoLINC demonstrated its new thermal interface material, handling 400 W/cm² of heat flux on warped silicon while keeping junction temperatures below 90°C, targeting AI data-center cooling.
Renesas released low-voltage GaN FETs for AI data centers and robotics.

Research
A Cornell-led team developed silicon-doped α-(AlxGa1−x)₂O₃ with a bandgap exceeding 7 eV while maintaining n-type conductivity, and fabricated both a Schottky diode and transistor using the ultra-wide-bandgap material. “Our achievement breaks the trend of increasing synthesis difficulty, cost and small size of ever-wider-bandgap semiconductors, for example, diamond and cubic boron nitride,” the researchers wrote.
UIUC, DOE’s NETL, and collaborators integrated a high-k oxide with 2D semiconductors using a carbon-dot monolayer as a van der Waals interface. The approach produced a smooth, stable gate dielectric with an equivalent oxide thickness of about 0.6 nm, low leakage and a high breakdown field, addressing a key challenge in scaling 2D transistors.
The U.S. DOE awarded $159M to 12 AI-driven scientific research projects, including a Fermilab-led effort to accelerate the design of microchips for extreme environments and a Harvard-led project combining AI and quantum hardware to advance quantum error correction.

Security
Hardware security releases

Lattice is collaborating with Arm and AMI on secure AI data-center infrastructure that combines Arm’s AGI CPU server platforms with Lattice FPGAs and AMI firmware.
Nuvoton and AMI launched a secure OpenBMC server-management platform built around Nuvoton’s Arbel BMC and AMI firmware.

Alerts and vulnerabilities

MediaTek disclosed 31 vulnerabilities across its chipsets, including two critical out-of-bounds-write flaws in modem components and high-severity issues affecting NeuroPilot, APU, and other subsystems.
Qualcomm detailed several high-severity chipset vulnerabilities, including a boot flaw that can bypass cryptographic-signature checks for certain partitions and a core-security issue involving page-table changes before secure-memory initialization.
CrowdStrike linked an AI attack of major South Korean financial institutions to a recently released open-source agentic penetration testing tool developed in China.

Government security news

The NSA released new Zero Trust guidance for securing critical operational-technology environments.
The GAO warned that federal agencies are not fully prepared for the transition to PQC, with many agencies still lacking complete inventories of vulnerable systems and adequate migration testing.
President Trump and executives from OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, and other AI companies signed a voluntary AI safety accord, committing to internal safeguards, independent evaluations, and board-level oversight. However, the agreement carries no regulatory penalties for noncompliance.

Security technical papers

Bit-Flip Attack Resilience in AI HW  (UF et al.)

Detecting Invariant Footprints of Microarchitectural Attacks (Texas A&M)
What the SW Hides About LLM Training Data, HW Reveals at Scale & Accelerators Magnify (NC State)

Vehicles, Batteries
Infineon debuted its new TRAVEO CYT4EN automotive MCU for high-performance instrument clusters and advanced cockpit graphics that could also be used in motorcycles.
Samsung’s System LSI division is reportedly halting its development of new automotive application processors amid cost pressures, Munhwa reported.
EVs

Honda and collaborators developed underlying technology for a wireless charging road system that could charge EVs, including heavy-duty trucks, while driving. The system uses power transmitters embedded in roadways and receivers installed in vehicles.
BMW debuted its new iX4 luxury electric SUV, with the vehicle reportedly offering fast charging and up to 514 miles in WLTP range.

Government Regulations

Tesla is continuing its push for EU approval of its full self-driving systems, with German officials now coming out in support of the technology. A Reuters investigation this week reviewed hundreds of emails between company officials and European safety regulators, examining the company’s efforts to accelerate regulatory approval amid questions over its safety claims.
U.S. regulators granted a five-year exemption allowing autonomous trucks to use flashing safety beacons instead of requiring drivers to place physical warning devices around stopped vehicles.
The EU is considering import restrictions on Chinese hybrid vehicles after Beijing rejected a request to voluntarily limit exports.
The UK is considering tariffs on Chinese EV imports to protect domestic automakers from lower-cost competition.
South Korea unveiled a $747B energy-transition plan targeting more than 70% of new vehicle sales from electric and hydrogen-powered vehicles by 2035.

Vehicle technical papers

Formal Security Analysis of CAN XL (Georgia Tech, QCRI, Purdue)
Radar Novel View Synthesis for Dynamic Driving Scenes (Technion)
Automotive HW Attacks: An Architect’s Guide to TARA (TTControl et al.)
Predictive Architecture For End-to-End Autonomous Driving (NYU)

Quantum
QC hardware

Infineon and Swiss quantum computing company ZuriQ AG expanded their quantum computing hardware collaboration to further scale quantum processing units for future commercial systems.
Infleqtion, Honeywell Aerospace, and UCSB collaborated on a new integrated optical cavity, built on silicon nitride, that reduces the space needed to keep lasers stable inside quantum systems, paving the way for miniaturization of quantum hardware.
IonQ demonstrated a photonic quantum interconnect linking a trapped-ion qubit with silicon-vacancy quantum memory at more than 1,000 entanglement events per second, over four times the previous reported trapped-ion record.

Investment, government initiatives

DARPA selected four companies to advance to the final stage of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative: Atom Computing for scalable arrays of neutral atoms; Diraq for Si CMOS spin qubits; IBM for modular superconducting processors; and IonQ for trapped-ion quantum computing.
PsiQuantum received a conditional loan commitment of up to $150M from the U.S. Department of War to expand its manufacturing and prototyping capabilities at the hub in Milpitas, California.
Universal Quantum raised over $100M to commercialize its modular technology with a path to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

Quantum technical papers

Error semitransparent universal control of a bosonic logical qubit (Cornell, Berkeley)
InAsSb surface quantum well w/in situ deposited Nb as a platform for hybrid devices (ETH Z.)

Workforce, Education
Purdue University launched a mobile semiconductor fabrication lab that brings hands-on lithography, deposition, and etching training directly to students and aspiring technicians without requiring access to a full cleanroom.
Cadence announced new Digital Badges, verified credentials issued through Credly, aimed at PCB and package design.
Government intervention

The NSF launched a program to create accelerated bachelor’s-to-Ph.D. pathways and interdisciplinary graduate training aimed at moving STEM graduates more quickly into critical technology fields.
The DHS proposed charging schools $70k for initial Optional Practical Training, which lets international graduates work in their field after college, and $30K for subsequent periods. The change could make it more expensive for chip companies to hire international engineering graduates.
A proposed U.S. bill would raise fines for willful H-1B violations from $5K to $100K, and for the most serious violations from $35K to $250K, while extending employer debarments.
